CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114732
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by an improper authentication vulnerability in multi-host installations. When a user logs in with an alias address, rcube_user::query() matched the address against identity records without qualifying the lookup by IMAP host, so a login could be resolved to a user account belonging to a different IMAP host. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix bug where an alias login wasn’t qualified by IMAP host”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114731
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the CSS proxy (the utils/modcss action). The fetched stylesheet was read into memory in full, with no size limit and no read timeout, so a stylesheet URL referencing an attacker-controlled host could be used to exhaust server memory. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Add a size limit to the CSS proxy content processing”, which caps the response at 5 MB, reads it as a stream and applies a read timeout.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114730
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail 1.6.14 before 1.6.20 and 1.7.0 before 1.7.5 is affected by a server-side request forgery filter bypass. The network blocklist used by rcube_utils::is_local_url() omitted the RFC 6052 NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96, the RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 and the unspecified address ::/128, so URLs such as http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/ passed the filter and reached loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix SSRF filter (is_local_url()) bypass via NAT64 64:ff9b::/96”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114729
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a remote content blocking bypass. rcube_washtml inspected the SVG SMIL animation attributes `to`, `from` and values for URIs, but not `by`; so markup such as in an HTML message caused remote content to be loaded without the user's consent, disclosing the client IP address and confirming that the message was opened. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix remote-content blocker bypass via SVG SMIL `by` attribute”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-113406
CVE.report.description: BA-Workflow developed by YS-infoware has a SQL Injection vulnerability. Authenticated remote attackers can inject arbitrary SQL statements to read, modify, and delete database contents.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-110354
CVE.report.description: HAProxy 3 before 3.4.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service (persistent worker-thread CPU exhaustion) via an HTTP/1.1 chunked request. Although the H1 multiplexer drains the request before closing the stream, the parser repeatedly re-processes the same bytes without making progress. The affected thread stays busy at 100% CPU after timeouts expire and after the client disconnects, and repeated requests can consume all worker threads until the process is restarted.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-110353
CVE.report.description: HAProxy 3.2 before 3.4.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service (worker-thread CPU exhaustion) via a truncated HTTP/2 PING frame. h2c_handle_ping in src/mux_h2.c does not check for a short read, unlike the other H2 frame handlers. Because the incomplete frame cannot be processed, its data is never consumed, and the H2 multiplexer tasklet is repeatedly woken by that pending data without making progress. The CPU spins until timeout http-request closes the connection, and an attacker opening many such connections can sustain high CPU usage.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-113405
CVE.report.description: BA-Workflow developed by YS-infoware has a SQL Injection vulnerability. Authenticated remote attackers can inject arbitrary SQL statements to read, modify, and delete database contents.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112329
CVE.report.description: The Sensei LMS WordPress plugin before 4.26.4 contains a broken access control vulnerability in the legacy save_new_message handler hooked on the init action, which validates only a generic nonce without verifying course enrollment or restricting post_id to valid post types. Authenticated attackers, including unprivileged Subscribers, can supply an arbitrary post_id for any course, lesson, or quiz to create a private message addressed to that post's author, bypassing the enrollment checks enforced by the newer REST send-message controller.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112293
CVE.report.description: BoxyHQ Enterprise SaaS Starter Kit through 1.6.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows non-owner team members to manage billing because payment routes skip the team_payments permission check. Authenticated MEMBER or ADMIN users can call create-portal-link, create-checkout-session, and products to open Stripe billing portals, view invoices, change payment methods, or alter subscriptions.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112288
CVE.report.description: Krayin CRM 2.2.5 before 2.2.7 contains a server-side request forgery filter bypass that allows users with webhook permissions to reach internal addresses via DNS rebinding. Attackers can return a public address during WebhookService::isSafeEndpoint() validation and an internal address when Guzzle re-resolves, sending blind requests to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112283

Attackers can supply a crafted .clpi file on a disc, image, or directory with a huge num_point to exhaust memory and CPU, causing denial of service.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112278

Attackers can send a raw bitmap cache order declaring large width, height, and bpp values with a tiny payload, causing memcpy() to read past the receive buffer and crash the client.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112273

Attackers can deliver crafted DNS packets whose additional, answer, or authority records trigger a one-byte read when parsed, crashing applications on hardened allocators.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112268

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-112077
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was detected in radareorg radare2 6.2.0/6.2.2. This issue affects the function r_core_cmd_str_pipe in the library libr/core/rtr_http.inc.c of the component HTTP Sandbox Policy Handler. Performing a manipulation results in protection mechanism failure. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The attack is considered to have high complexity. The exploitability is assessed as difficult. Upgrading to version 6.2.4 is capable of addressing this issue. The patch is named 18fd12efa98a7d1977de7bdd379d8a848777b90f. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The pre-requisite of the vulnerability is reflected by the CVSS vector. One of the project maintainers explains: "There is a real sandbox configuration issue here, but the report overstates it. The HTTP server defaults to http.sandbox=true, so commands received through /cmd temporarily enable cfg.sandbox. However, cfg.sandbox.grain defaults to all, which means all sandbox capabilities - including exec - remain allowed. Therefore enabling the HTTP sandbox alone does NOT prevent commands from spawning processes. This only matters when the HTTP command endpoint is reachable by someone you do not trust. It is not a remote vulnerability by default: the HTTP server must first be started and exposed to the attacker."

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114728
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a remote content blocking bypass in the handling of FuncIRI attributes. rcube_washtml detected the CSS url() token with a pattern that enumerated only some of its escaped spellings, so values using other CSS escape sequences, for example \000075rl( or u\72 l(, were not recognized and remote content was loaded from an HTML message without the user's consent. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix remote content blocking bypass via CSS escapes in FuncIRI attributes (again)”, which resolves CSS escapes before matching and also inspects the `to`, `from` and `by` attributes.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114727
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 passes potentially unsafe content into ImageMagick when resizing images. SVG and EPS were accepted as valid image types for contact photo upload and conversion, and both formats can reference external resources and invoke ImageMagick delegates when processed. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix passing potentally unsafe attachment content into ImageMagick on image resize”, which removes svg and eps from the accepted types.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114726
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a mail header injection vulnerability in the Bounce (resend) action. rcube_mime::decode_address_list() did not strip control characters from the decoded display name, so a received message whose From display-name carries CRLF sequences in an encoded word could inject arbitrary headers into the message emitted when the user bounces it. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix mail header injection via the From display-name in the Bounce (resend) action”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114725
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a mail header injection vulnerability. rcmail_sendmail stripped newline characters only from the Subject and Organization headers, leaving other header values taken from request parameters unsanitized, so a remote authenticated attacker could inject arbitrary headers into an outgoing message via the References, In-Reply-To, Message-ID and From parameters. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix mail header injection via References/In-Reply-To/Message-ID/From parameters”, which normalizes whitespace in every string header value.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114724
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 contains an object injection primitive in rcube_session::unserialize(). A session key prefixed with “!” was treated as having no value, and the reconstructed serialized string was emitted with a key but no corresponding value, desynchronizing the remainder of the input so that following session data was interpreted as a serialized value. This yields a PHP object injection primitive for an attacker able to influence stored session data. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix object injection primitive in rcube_session::unserialize() via “!”-prefixed session keys”, which rejects such keys.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114723
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 allows the ImageMagick resource limits to be bypassed during thumbnail generation. When rcube_image falls back to GD, the available-memory check was applied only on Windows, so on other platforms a crafted image with large dimensions was processed by GD without any resource limit and could exhaust server memory. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix ImageMagick resource limits bypass by GD fallback during thumbnail generation”, which applies the memory check on all platforms.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114722
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a CSS scoping bypass in HTML messages. rcube_utils::mod_css_styles() did not treat an at-rule prologue such as @layer a; as a selector boundary, and did not handle selectors beginning with ::, so selectors following an at-rule were left unscoped and applied to the whole Roundcube interface instead of being confined to the message body. This allows an HTML message to restyle application chrome for UI redressing and spoofing. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix CSS scoping bypass in HTML messages using at-rules”.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114721
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 allows the disabled_actions configuration setting to be bypassed. The check compared only the action name as requested, so a remote authenticated attacker could reach an action listed in disabled_actions by requesting it through its deprecated alias instead. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix bug where deprecated action aliases bypassed `disabled_actions` setting”, which moves the check into rcmail::action_handler() and resolves aliases before comparing.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114720
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by an IMAP command injection vulnerability. A remote authenticated attacker can exploit this via CRLF sequences injected into the _flag parameter of the mail/mark action to execute arbitrary IMAP commands. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix IMAP command injection via CRLF in `_flag` parameter of mail/mark action”, which rejects flags containing control, whitespace and IMAP-special characters.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114719
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a CSRF validation bypass in the mark-as-junk action of the markasjunk plugin. The plugin read the _uid parameter from POST data but passed it to rcmail::get_uids() without constraining the input mode, so values re-read inside that helper could be taken from the query string and the action carried out without a valid CSRF token. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix CSRF validation bypass in the mark-as-junk action”, which passes rcube_utils::INPUT_POST explicitly.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114718
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the password plugin. Error text returned by a password driver was concatenated into the message presented to the user without HTML escaping, so a backend able to influence that text, such as the DirectAdmin API, could inject script into the Roundcube interface. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix XSS issue in handling of password driver error responses”, which escapes the driver message before display.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114717
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a mail header injection vulnerability when a message is forwarded as an attachment. The subject of the forwarded message was used verbatim to generate the attachment name, so a received message whose subject contains CRLF sequences could inject arbitrary MIME part headers into the outgoing message. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix mail header injection via subject of a message forwarded as attachment”, which collapses whitespace in the generated name.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114716
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by a mail header injection vulnerability. rcmail_sendmail::extract_inline_images() used the media type taken from an inline image data URI without validating it, so a remote authenticated attacker could inject arbitrary MIME part headers into the outgoing message by placing CRLF sequences in that media type. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix mail header injection via media type in an inline image data URI”, which validates the media type with rcube_mime::is_mimetype_valid().

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114715
CVE.report.description: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 is affected by an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Modoboa driver of the password plugin. The driver took the first entry of the account search result returned by the Modoboa API instead of matching the authenticated user, so a password change could be applied to a different account. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix bug where Password Modoboa driver could change password for another account”, which selects the account whose username matches and fails if none does.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114664
CVE.report.description: Frappe Framework before 16.33.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events method, which fails to properly neutralize user-supplied input before including it in SQL queries. Authenticated attackers can send crafted input to get_events and infer query results from application behavior to extract sensitive database information.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114661
CVE.report.description: OpenRemote 1.2.0 before 1.31.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in GatewayServiceResource that allows any authenticated user to start, stop and query gateway tunnels without an administrative role. Attackers can send POST or DELETE requests to the gateway tunnel endpoint to open persistent bidirectional TCP circuits into an edge gateway's network or tear down operator tunnels.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114660
CVE.report.description: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.5 contains an improper access control vulnerability in FlexDirectory::dynamicFlexField() that allows page authors to call arbitrary Flex object methods via flex-*@ directives in page frontmatter. When a user with page edit rights opens the page, directives calling setStorageKey() and delete() run in their session, deleting protected pages neither account may delete.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114659
CVE.report.description: Grav Flex Objects plugin 1.4.0 before 1.4.17 contains an authorization bypass because its generic /api/v1/flex-objects/pages API routes check only directory-level admin.pages permissions, without enforcing the Pages API's api.pages.read/write permissions or page-level permissions rules. Authenticated non-super users with api.access and admin.pages or admin.configuration.pages permissions can read page source and frontmatter, modify content, or delete pages they are denied.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114658
CVE.report.description: Grav Login plugin from 3.6.0 before 3.9.13 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the login.invite task that allows page authors to obtain super user accounts. Attackers can define an invitation form granting super access in page frontmatter, submit it unauthenticated, and register the invited address for full site control.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114657
CVE.report.description: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.5 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows page authors to capture visitors' HTTP Basic credentials through Twig page content. Authors can print the request Uri object, which embeds PHP_AUTH_USER and PHP_AUTH_PW, inside an inline style background image to exfiltrate administrators' credentials to an external host.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114656
CVE.report.description: Traefik before 2.11.58 and 3.7.13 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated clients to skip client-certificate checks because negated Host matchers are counted as served domains. Attackers can reach backends protected by RequireAndVerifyClientCert when a router rule with !Host() creates a TLS options conflict that falls back to the default options.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114642
CVE.report.description: Traefik 2.11.0 before 2.11.58 and 3.0.0 before 3.7.14 stores its NTLM/Kerberos backend round tripper in a client-connection slot not keyed by ServersTransport, so one service's TLS client configuration is reused for another service's backend. An unauthenticated client can arm the slot via a backend issuing an NTLM or Negotiate challenge, then reach another service on the same keep-alive connection, bypassing its root CAs, server name, and certificate verification.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114641
CVE.report.description: Traefik 2.11.x before 2.11.58 and 3.x before 3.7.14 contains a race condition in NTLM and Kerberos (Negotiate) backend authentication, where the per-connection sticky round tripper slot is read and written without synchronization. Remote attackers can send concurrent HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 requests over one connection to orphan backend connections, break connection-bound authentication, or crash Traefik.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114640
CVE.report.description: Traefik from v3.7.0 before v3.7.14 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in its Kubernetes Ingress-NGINX provider that forwards client-supplied Ssl-Client-* headers on the plaintext HTTP router. When ssl-redirect is disabled alongside auth-tls-pass-certificate-to-upstream, unauthenticated attackers can send Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a chosen certificate subject and issuer to impersonate mTLS identities.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114639
CVE.report.description: Traefik 2.11.0 before 2.11.58 and 3.0.0 before 3.7.14 contains an authentication bypass because a first request preauthenticated with an Authorization: Negotiate token authenticates a socket in the globally shared backend connection pool, which is never isolated. Unauthenticated attackers on separate frontend connections can be assigned that NTLM/Kerberos-bound socket and perform reads or writes with the victim's identity.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114638
CVE.report.description: Traefik v3.7.0 before v3.7.14 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider that merges client CAs when auth-tls-secret names collide after dot-to-dash normalization. Attackers holding certificates from another host's CA can access a host requiring its own client CA, while that host's legitimate clients are refused.

Description :HAProxy 3 before 3.4.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service (persistent worker-thread CPU exhaustion) via an HTTP/1.1 chunked request. cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-110353 - HAProxy HTTP/2 PING Frame Denial of Service
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110353
Published : Oct. 22, 2026, 3:16 a.m. | 35 minutes ago
Description :HAProxy 3.2 before 3.4.6 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service (worker-thread CPU exhaustion) via a truncated HTTP/2 PING frame. h2c_handle_ping in src/mux_h2.c does not check for a short read, unlike the other H2 frame handlers. Because the incomplete frame cannot be processed, its data is never consumed, and the H2 multiplexer tasklet is repeatedly woken by that pending data without making progress. Description :In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4 and 10.2.8, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could derive the PostgreSQL sidecar database superuser password and run arbitrary operating system commands as the user account running Splunk Enterprise on search head cluster members. For more information see About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access), server.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.2/configuration-file-reference/10.2.0-configuration-file-reference/server.conf), and Sidecar configuration settings (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/splunk-sidecars/sidecar-configuration-settings) in the Splunk documentation.
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

Published : Oct. 21, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 4 hours, 32 minutes ago
Description :In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user that holds a role with the schedule_search capability could bypass the expected safeguards in the scheduled search workflow. cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-103090 - Unauthenticated Biscuit Credential Disclosure via GET /enroll/status in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM)
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-103090
Published : Oct. 21, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 4 hours, 32 minutes ago
Description :Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) and Insufficiently Protected Credentials (CWE-522) in the control plane enrollment status handler (HandleEnrollStatus at GET /enroll/status in internal/controlplane/server.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to retrieve an approved bootstrap-enrolled peer's signed Biscuit identity token by supplying a peer_id obtainable from the unauthenticated GET /info endpoint. A related flaw in POST /enroll allowed any bootstrap-token holder to re-fetch another peer's credential. An attacker can replay the disclosed Biscuit token as a bearer credential on /policies to read mesh authorization policies and on /routers/lease to overwrite advertised router multiaddrs. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.9 or later, which requires cryptographic proof of possession of the enrollment private key on credential-releasing endpoints, enforces rate limiting, and validates router lease addresses.
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

Description :Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511, 8u511-perf, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, 27.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21 and 21.0.13; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data as well as unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-96640 - Pillow PDF append accepts malformed shared page-tree DAG causing resource exhaustion
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-96640
Published : Oct. 21, 2026, 9:20 p.m. | 6 hours, 29 minutes ago
Description :Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.1.0 until 13.0.0, PdfParser.linearize_page_tree() in src/PIL/PdfParser.py treats a PDF /Pages graph as a tree without tracking duplicate indirect references. When Image.save(..., format="PDF", append=True) processes an attacker-controlled existing PDF whose /Kids arrays repeatedly reference the same child /Pages node, Pillow expands the shared subtree as distinct pages. A compact malformed PDF can therefore create exponentially many page references and consume disproportionate CPU before the append completes. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
Severity: 8.2 | HIGH

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-96639 - Pillow multi-frame loaders can reuse stale native image storage after mode transitions
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-96639
Published : Oct. 21, 2026, 9:20 p.m. | 6 hours, 29 minutes ago
Description :Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 11.0.0 until 13.0.0, multi-frame loaders can retain an ImagingCore allocation created for a narrow frame mode while a later frame of the same dimensions changes the logical mode and decoder tiles to wider RGB or CMYK data. ImageFile.load_prepare() reuses the stale native storage because _im is non-null without verifying that its mode and size still match. Crafted PSD, MPO, DCX, or MIC frame transitions can then write wider pixels into the narrow allocation, causing native out-of-bounds writes and crashes. The MPO path can also cause a native over-read and, in demonstrated runtime-specific profiles, command execution. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
Severity: 9.8 | CRITICAL

FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.title: Atlassian Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability
FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.description:
CVE-2026-21589 is a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting multiple Atlassian Data Center products, including Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, and Fisheye. The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within an affected application's web root directory.
Exploitation requires the attacker to know the exact name and path of the target file in advance. The vulnerability does not provide directory listing or file enumeration capabilities by itself. Depending on the files exposed and the application configuration, successful exploitation could disclose sensitive information and potentially support further attacks.

FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.title: GitLab Path Traversal Vulnerability
FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.description:
FortiGuard Labs has observed attack activity targeting CVE-2026-85706, a critical path traversal vulnerability in GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition. The vulnerability affects the repository commits API and can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to read arbitrary files from a vulnerable GitLab server due to improper path confinement and missing authentication enforcement. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 10.0 and requires no privileges or user interaction.

CVE-2026-85706 was added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 11, 2026. Public exploit and proof-of-concept material has also emerged, increasing the potential for exploitation against exposed, unpatched GitLab instances.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP, a widely used server-side scripting language that powers websites and web applications. They involve flaws in PHP's internal request-processing and memory-management behavior that can be triggered when handling malicious requests. Both are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities rated as 9.2 (CVSS 4.0).

• CVE-2026-109618 - RCE via out-of-memory corruption: An out-of-memory condition can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Subsequent request-cleanup operations may incorrectly process this invalid data, potentially enabling remote code execution.

• CVE-2026-109619 - RCE via stale global state: Internal request state can persist after its associated memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may access this stale state before normal initialization resets it, potentially enabling remote code execution.

Successful exploitation could compromise the PHP application process and potentially provide access to sensitive server resources, application data, or databases, depending on the permissions of the affected process and the surrounding environment.

PHP announced emergency security updates for October 21, 2026, following reports that details of the vulnerabilities had leaked ahead of the planned disclosure. Subsequent reports highlighted ongoing exploit research and potential attack activity, underscoring the urgency of applying the available patches. However, widespread exploitation of either vulnerability has not been independently confirmed.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP installations that process web requests, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. PHP identifies Apache deployments using mod_php as particularly at risk because a demonstrated exploit can trigger before application code runs.

Organizations should prioritize patching internet-facing PHP servers and other exposed deployments immediately.
1. Apply the security updates. Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, as appropriate. Organizations using vendor-maintained packages should apply the corresponding security updates from their distributions or service providers.
2. Reduce exposure until patching is complete. Where immediate remediation is not possible, isolate affected systems from untrusted networks or temporarily disable exposed services when operationally feasible.
3. Review request-processing limits. Apply appropriate web-server or reverse-proxy limits for request sizes, input fields, multipart sections, headers, and nesting depth. These controls can reduce exposure but are not a substitute for patching.
4. Review potentially vulnerable systems. Investigate suspicious web requests, unexpected PHP worker behavior, unexplained process execution, and unusual access to application files or databases. Prioritize internet-facing systems and investigate potential compromise before returning affected services to production.

PHP 8.1 and older are no longer supported by the PHP project and do not receive its standard security updates. Organizations using these versions should check whether their operating-system vendor provides backported fixes or migrate to a supported release.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs recommends a defense-in-depth approach to reduce exposure to attacks targeting vulnerable PHP deployments and is currently monitoring the situation and will provide updates as new information becomes available and additional protections are released.

• FortiGuard Labs has virtual patches available for the vulnerabilities ( CVE-2026-109619 & CVE-2026-109618 ) released in version 37.316.

https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/otips/10009977
https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/otips/10009978

• FortiCNAPP Vulnerability Management Service: Detects CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in PHP packages installed from Linux distribution repositories. Ubuntu, Debian, and Alpine Linux 3.24 have published fixes. RHEL and its rebuilds, Amazon Linux, and SUSE have not yet published fixes; accordingly, findings for these distributions may not include a fixed version until the respective vendors release updates.

• FortiGuard Web Application Firewall (FortiWeb): Where applicable, review web application protection policies and request inspection controls to help identify or block malicious HTTP requests. These controls should not be considered a replacement for the PHP security updates.

• FortiGuard Antivirus and Behavior Detection: Use available malware detection and behavioral protections to help identify suspicious payloads or post-exploitation activity associated with a compromised web server.

• FortiGuard Incident Response: If exploitation is suspected, investigate the affected server, identify potential persistence mechanisms, determine whether sensitive data or credentials were accessed, and contain any confirmed compromise.

• For information on Fortinet products affected by this vulnerability, please refer to the Fortinet PSIRT Advisory (FG-IR-26-186). PSIRT | FortiGuard Labs

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Atlassian Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack? CVE-2026-21589 is a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting multiple Atlassian Data Center and Server products. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within an affected application's web root, provided the attacker knows the exact file path and name.

The vulnerability stems from improper restrictions on access to files within the web application root. Successful exploitation could expose sensitive files and potentially provide information useful for further attacks, depending on the affected application's configuration and the files accessible.

The vulnerability requires no authentication or user interaction, making internet-facing deployments a priority for remediation.
What is the recommended Mitigation? Atlassian published its security advisory on October 5, 2026, and recommends immediate remediation for affected installations. Atlassian recommends that you patch each of your affected installations to fixed versions or the latest version.
What FortiGuard Coverage is available? • FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor CVE-2026-21589 and associated attack activity. We will provide updates as new intelligence, detections, and protections become available.
• FortiGuard Labs has released an IPS signature to detect and protect against attack attempts targeting CVE-2026-21589 affecting multiple Atlassian Data Center and Server products.
• FortiGuard Labs recommends applying the security updates provided by Atlassian to affected products.
• FortiGuard Antivirus & Behavior Detection detects and blocks malicious files, web shells, and other payloads that may be delivered following successful exploitation.
• FortiGuard Web Filtering blocks access to known malicious domains, command-and-control infrastructure, and payload-hosting locations associated with post-exploitation activity.
• FortiGuard IoC Service helps identify known indicators of compromise and malicious infrastructure associated with related threats.
• FortiEDR provides endpoint detection and response capabilities to help identify suspicious post-exploitation activity on potentially compromised systems.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-day Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

Threat actors are actively exploiting two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances. Citrix confirmed that both vulnerabilities were exploited in the wild before security updates were available. CISA has subsequently added both vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog and reported that threat intelligence confirms exploitation globally.

CVE-2026-88771 is an improper input validation vulnerability that can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands. It affects NetScaler deployments without requiring an additional feature to be enabled. CVE-2026-88772 is a memory overflow vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution or denial-of-service conditions. It affects appliances with DTLS enabled, which is enabled by default for VPN virtual servers. Both vulnerabilities have a CVSS v4 score of 9.5.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should immediately identify exposed NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances and apply the security updates provided by Citrix. Fixed releases include NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1-73.37 and later and 13.1-64.23 and later, with corresponding updates for FIPS and NDcPP builds.

Because both vulnerabilities were exploited as zero-days before patches were available, patching alone should not be treated as confirmation that an appliance was not compromised. Organizations should review NetScaler and supporting security logs for suspicious activity, preserve forensic evidence where compromise is suspected, and investigate the appliance before making changes that could destroy evidence.

If compromise is suspected, organizations should isolate the affected appliance, review administrative and outbound connections, investigate for persistence, and consider resetting credentials, invalidating sessions, and replacing potentially exposed certificates or keys.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor this vulnerability and associated attack activity. We will provide updates as new intelligence, detections, and protections become available.
• FortiGuard Labs has released an IPS signature to detect and protect against attack attempts targeting CVE-2026-88771 vulnerability. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs
• FortiGuard Labs has released an IPS signature to detect and protect against attack attempts targeting CVE-2026-88772 vulnerability. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs
• FortiGuard Antivirus & Behavior Detection detects and blocks malicious files, web shells, and other payloads that may be delivered following successful exploitation.
• FortiGuard Web Filtering blocks access to known malicious domains, command-and-control infrastructure, and payload-hosting locations associated with post-exploitation activity.
• FortiGuard IoC Service can help identify known indicators associated with compromise and malicious infrastructure.
• FortiEDR provides endpoint detection and response capabilities for suspicious post-exploitation activity on systems that may be affected following compromise.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway RCE
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

FortiGuard Labs has observed active network telemetry relating to CVE-2025-7775, a memory overflow vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway that enables remote code execution (RCE) and denial of service (DoS) under certain pre-conditions. Exploitation on unpatched appliances has been confirmed, and CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Citrix advisories also address:

CVE-2025-7776 – a memory overflow issue causing DoS when NetScaler is configured as a Gateway (PCoIP).

CVE-2025-8424 – an improper access control flaw affecting the management interface.

Recent industry reporting highlights that adversaries increasingly leverage AI-driven exploit development frameworks such as Hexstrike-AI, which integrate large language models (LLMs) with fuzzing and orchestration. These toolchains reduce the time from disclosure to weaponized zero-day exploitation, increasing the urgency for patching.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances are strongly recommended to:

- Review and follow the official Citrix security bulletins.
- Apply all relevant patches and updates as soon as possible.
- Monitor for any suspicious activity, such as dropped web shells or abnormal memory behavior.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

  • Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): FortiGuard IPS Service is available to detect and block exploit attempts targeting CVE-2025-7775. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs

  • Web Application Security: FortiGuard Web Security Service is available to detect and block exploit activity. Web Application Security | FortiGuard Labs

  • Incident Response Service: The FortiGuard Incident Response team is available to assist with any suspected compromise.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: GitLab Path Traversal vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

FortiGuard Labs has observed attack activity targeting CVE-2026-85706, a critical path traversal vulnerability in GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition. The vulnerability affects the repository commits API and can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to read arbitrary files from a vulnerable GitLab server due to improper path confinement and missing authentication enforcement. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 10.0 and requires no privileges or user interaction.

FortiGuard telemetry observed over the last 7 days shows attack activity targeting CVE-2026-85706 across multiple countries and industries. The most targeted countries include Belarus, South Korea, Germany, the People’s Republic of China, and Thailand, while the most targeted industries include Education, Technology, Telco/Carrier, Media/Communications, and Banking/Finance/Insurance.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Affected versions include:
GitLab 18.7 to before 19.1.8
GitLab 19.2 to before 19.2.6
GitLab 19.3 to before 19.3.2

• Upgrade immediately to GitLab 19.1.8, 19.2.6, 19.3.2, or later, as applicable.
• Prioritize externally exposed GitLab instances for remediation.
• Restrict unnecessary Internet exposure of GitLab services.
• Review GitLab and web-server logs for unexpected requests to repository/API endpoints.
• Investigate potentially exposed credentials, configuration files, tokens, and other sensitive information if exploitation is suspected.
• Rotate credentials or secrets that may have been accessible from the GitLab server.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard IPS Service: FortiGuard IPS signature 62167 detects and blocks network-based exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-85706. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs
• FortiGate: Offers IPS protection to help prevent exploitation attempts against vulnerable GitLab deployments.
• FortiGuard Vulnerability Management: Helps identify vulnerable assets and prioritize remediation based on exposure and risk.
• FortiEDR: Offers additional endpoint detection and response capabilities if exploitation leads to suspicious activity on the underlying GitLab server.
• FortiGuard Incident Response Service: Assists organizations in investigating potential compromise, determining the scope of attacker activity, and supporting containment, remediation, and recovery efforts following exploitation.

Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.title: PHP core RCE vulnerability patches (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.8

CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).
